title: Clone for Sharing
story: When you need to share a document with two departments, you make a photocopy. Clone is your photocopier — it creates independent copies so everyone gets their own.
why: Clone is the deliberate escape hatch from move semantics — use it when you genuinely need multiple independent owners of the same data.
analogy: Clone is like photocopying a document — every department gets their own copy, and changes to one copy don't affect the others.
try_it: Create a string, clone it, modify the clone, and verify the original is unchanged. This proves clones are independent.
tips: Clone gives you a deep, independent copy — changes don't propagate
Prefer borrowing (&) over cloning for read-only access — it's zero-cost
Clone is explicit — you always know when expensive copies happen
Consider whether a function really needs ownership before cloning for it
common_mistakes: Cloning when a borrow would work — cloning large structures is expensive
Thinking clones share data — they don't, each clone is fully independent
Cloning inside loops — the cost multiplies with every iteration
